headline: Looking for something to do this weekend? Here are the Top 5 local events for Oct. 24-25
teaser: A free science festival in Fort Pierce, trick-or-treating in Stuart, a Tradition fall market, Sunday jazz and a guided bat hike lead this weekend's Treasure Coast picks.
body:
With Halloween just around the corner, this weekend's Treasure Coast calendar has plenty to offer beyond the usual routine. A major hands-on science festival heads to a new Fort Pierce venue, downtown Stuart welcomes families for an early round of trick-or-treating, and Tradition hosts an afternoon of fall festivities. Sunday's picks range from free jazz in the park to an evening search for bats along a preserve trail.

Here are five standout events for **Saturday, Oct. 24, and Sunday, Oct. 25**, across Martin and St. Lucie counties.

## 1. Indian River Lagoon Science Festival, Fort Pierce

**When:** Saturday, Oct. 24, 10 a.m.-3 p.m. **Where:** Museum Pointe Park, 414 Seaway Drive, Fort Pierce. **Admission:** Free.

The 11th annual Indian River Lagoon Science Festival brings hands-on experiments, demonstrations and local science organizations together for a day of discovery. More than 50 exhibitors are expected, with activities covering science, technology, engineering, art and math. Organizers highlight marine mammal rescue, sea turtles, underwater robots and even a chance to learn how crime-scene investigators work.

**Important location change:** This year's festival is at Museum Pointe Park, between the St. Lucie County Aquarium and the regional history center, rather than its previous location. Organizers also list free parking at Causeway Cove Marina, along with complimentary admission to the aquarium and history center during the festival. [Festival details](https://visitstlucie.com/event/2026-indian-river-lagoon-science-festival/).

## 2. Hobgoblins on Main Street, Stuart

**When:** Saturday, Oct. 24, noon-3 p.m. **Where:** Riverwalk Stage and surrounding historic downtown Stuart. **Admission:** Free.

Downtown Stuart is getting into the Halloween spirit with the 27th annual Hobgoblins on Main Street, presented by Stuart Main Street and the Historic Downtown Business Association. The afternoon is designed around family-friendly, safe trick-or-treating, giving children a chance to celebrate Halloween a week early.

With the activity centered around downtown's Riverwalk Stage, this is an easy choice for families who want an afternoon outing without traveling far between stops. [Event details](https://stuartmainstreet.org/events/hobgoblins-on-main/).

## 3. IL Merchato Fall-O-Ween Market, Port St. Lucie

**When:** Saturday, Oct. 24, 1-7 p.m. **Where:** Tradition Square, SW Meeting Street, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Free general admission.

Tradition Square will host a fall and Halloween-themed market with local vendors, food trucks and activities for children. Organizers list trick-or-treating, bounce houses, face painting, costumed character meet-and-greets and a seasonal photo booth among the attractions.

The event offers a longer afternoon-to-evening window than many of Saturday's activities, making it another option for families planning around the day's other commitments. Costumes are encouraged. [Event details](https://traditionfl.com/events/il-merchato-fall-o-ween-market/).

## 4. Sunday Jazz in the Park, Stuart

**When:** Sunday, Oct. 25, 3-6 p.m. **Where:** Memorial Park, 300 SE Ocean Blvd., Stuart. **Admission:** Free.

The nonprofit Music4Unity is kicking off its fifth season of Sunday Jazz in the Park with an afternoon of contemporary jazz and classic R&B. DJ Celo is scheduled to start the music at 3 p.m., followed by a live performance from the Charles Jones Trio at 5 p.m.

Visitors are encouraged to bring lawn chairs, blankets and coolers to settle in under the park's banyan trees. For anyone looking for a relaxed Sunday afternoon rather than another Halloween event, this is one of the weekend's strongest options. [Concert details](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/sunday-jazz-in-the-park-tickets-2003268022582).

## 5. Going Batty Full Moon Hike, Port St. Lucie

**When:** Sunday, Oct. 25, 6:30-8 p.m. **Where:** Spruce Bluff Preserve, 611 Dar Lane, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Check the organizer for registration and participation details.

Sunday evening offers a different kind of seasonal adventure: a guided nature outing in search of Florida's bats. Participants will look for bats flying, roosting or making calls along the trail while learning about their place in the local ecosystem.

The program is described as appropriate for **ages 8 and older**. It is a fitting way to close a Halloween-season weekend, particularly for families interested in wildlife rather than costumes and candy. Review participation requirements before heading to the preserve. [Hike details](https://visitstlucie.com/event/going-batty-full-moon-hike/).

Schedules and participation details can change, so check with organizers before leaving home. For more activities throughout Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, browse the [Treasure Coast Today events calendar](https://treasurecoast.today/events.html).
